independent_analysis: Direct local reconstruction using NumPy for candidate search only; exact original OAM high-table, SNES planar 4bpp decode, CGRAM BGR555, palette-zero transparency and pinned MesenCE 5-to-8 conversion. Zero additional emulator execution. The existing repo producer's full original-source archive reader is separately unit-tested; this numeric result is independently derived from real archived bytes.
observations: The historical 76..170 X window excludes all actual post-countdown red source sprite pixel matches; expanded X0..192 finds exactly 128..134 at screen origin X34,Y48.
Both horizontal windows find identical blue exact-match counts 277..282, at X82..86,Y158; widening X alone is not the source of its incomplete correspondence.
Measured red screen candidate X34 differs from held OAM x48; this source-derived displacement is not explained by a single held scanline225 OAM image.

The real source-wide red counts agree with the prior independent postcountdown exploratory counts of PR #3077. This fixes an existing matcher boundary condition, but does not restore full red or blue source pixel correspondence.

Colour-selective controls show red 6..12 chromatic exact matches despite 59..66 source chromatic pixels, whereas blue matches essentially all chromatic source pixels (71/71,73/74,61/61,69/69,62/62). Prior red 128..134 opaque matches are too gray-dominated to assert authentic red screen-pixel ownership.

independent_colour_discriminators.method: For each decoded original source 2D OBJ, count exact source RGB matches at wide-window best placement after restricting to opaque pixels with max(R,G,B)-min(R,G,B) >=35. For held red OBJ the chromatic pixels are strongly red (R>G+30 and R>B+30). Screen matches are still raw colour coincidences, not per-pixel ownership.
interpretation: Blue discriminative chromatic pixels match 71/71,73/74,61/61,69/69,62/62 across source ticks 1601..1605; held blue 2D pose is strongly frame-synchronous, without claiming finished PPU ownership.

Red same-viewport opaque RGB matches 128..134 versus wrong-viewport 106..116, and only 6..12 of 59..66 strongly red pixels match. Thus much of the red score comes from common greys and does not justify a validated original source 2D pose-to-screen identity.
Red chromatic-only exhaustive bounded screen-origin search over X0..192, upper Y0..110 yields at most 10,10,12,10,10 matches respectively, never a high-confidence recovery of the source red raster.

The original screen visibly contains overlay and course graphics intersecting the candidate 64x64 areas; whether any particular source red pixel was occluded versus not fetched is unknown without actual PPU draw/fetch timing.

cross_frame_local_registration.method: For each source sprite at bridge ticks 1601..1605, compare its exact opaque RGB against each five authentic completed screen P6 frames, optimizing only within ±8 pixels around same-frame source-derived screen position (blue X82..86/Y158; red X34/Y48). Uses true original CGRAM and source raster at each producer tick. This is a bounded heuristic temporal discriminator, not full per-scanline pixel ownership.
cross_frame_local_registration.finding: Blue uniquely favors each corresponding source tick. Red varies by a few gray-dominated matches across adjacent screens; no uniform ±1-frame red registration makes the held red raster fully match.
